clue.text: Ahead of time? No — so dust manically aiming for neat condition

indicators.note: dust flung about manically is thrown into wild disorder, so the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A frantic cleaner, too late to begin with, dusts like mad in pursuit of a tidy home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is an old word for cattle, so 'neat condition' is a disease of livestock; the tidy-house reading is the trap. The anagram uses every letter of AHEAD OF TIME NO SO DUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means cattle, and this notifiable viral illness affects cattle and other cloven-hoofed animals.

clue.text: Keep quiet when among ardent swimmers here

indicators.note: among says the quietening sound goes inside the word for ardent

parts.note: ardent means fiery, passionate
SH is the call to keep quiet

explanation.surface: Passionate swimmers are told to hush when they are in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishery is a stretch of water where fish, the swimmers, are bred or caught.

clue.text: Riding beast of burden is Aristotle

parts.note: riding a horse means being on it
an ass is a donkey, a classic beast of burden
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Greek philosopher is pictured astride a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The philosopher is a red herring: the Aristotle meant is the Greek shipping magnate.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle Onassis was the Greek shipping tycoon who married Jacqueline Kennedy.

clue.text: Man by joiner in a whirl? The reverse

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in puts the multiplication sign and the joining word inside the turned dance
the reverse tells us to turn the word for whirl back to front

parts.note: a reel is a whirling dance
by as in 'two by four' is the times sign X
and is the word that joins two items

explanation.surface: A man standing beside a carpenter caught up in a spin, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The reverse' turns REEL into LEER, which then holds X and AND: A + LE(XAND)ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander is a man's given name, borne by Alexander the Great among others.

clue.text: China ran up tab in absence of Jack

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for ran is written bottom to top

parts.note: ran away means fled

indicators.note: in absence of tells us to take the sailor out of the word tab

parts.note: taken as written
a jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

explanation.surface: A customer has run up a bill while the barman Jack is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FLED into DELF; TAB without AB leaves T.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is tin-glazed earthenware from the Dutch town, a kind of china.

clue.text: Natural? Close, but no cigar, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone guesses the word natural and is told they are close but miss out on the prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close, but' just completes the stock phrase; the letters of NO CIGAR are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is grown naturally, without artificial chemicals.

clue.text: Double-cross? Well, almost double-cross!

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: a double cross is XX, and X is the times sign, so two times

explanation.surface: A betrayal is described, then corrected to nearly a betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'double-cross' is read as two crosses, XX, each X a times sign: TWO TIMES, shortened by 'almost'.
explanation.definitionFit: To two-time someone is to deceive a partner by seeing someone else, a romantic double-cross.

clue.text: Fools wasting time on North Carolina headland? Spanning the years, this is characteristic

indicators.note: wasting means using up and losing the letter for time

parts.note: fools are idiots

indicators.note: spanning means the two year letters stretch either side of what follows

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year, so years plural gives two of them
NC is the US postal code for North Carolina
a ras is a headland, from the Arabic, common in crosswords

explanation.surface: Idiots linger on a Carolina cape for years, which is just like them.
explanation.walkthrough: IDIOTS less T gives IDIOS; then Y + NC RAS + Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiosyncrasy is a peculiar trait or quirk of a person, a distinctive characteristic.

clue.text: See 1
Franglais speaker at wedding needs this for footsie

parts.note: Franglais mixes French and English, so here the French article le
the groom traditionally makes a speech at the wedding reception

explanation.surface: A Frenchman mangling English at a wedding needs space under the table to play footsie.
explanation.walkthrough: In Franglais the bridegroom would be 'le groom', a French article on an English word.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing footsie under a table needs space for the legs, which is legroom.

clue.text: Amongst others, I snog nth sloven with oomph

definitions.note: the vowel sound I is one example among many

indicators.note: a sloven is untidy, so these letters are left in a messy new order

explanation.surface: A scruffy lover snogs with gusto, among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' links the second batch of fodder; the definition is the letter I as one of many single vowel sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A monophthong is a pure single vowel sound, of which an I sound is one example.

clue.text: Foreign poetry mentioned in old article

indicators.note: in puts the poetry between the abbreviation for old and the article

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
poetry when referred to is verse

explanation.surface: Some exotic verse gets a mention in an ancient piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversea, like overseas, describes something from abroad, so foreign.

clue.text: What daring trapeze artist wants is held back, causing strain

indicators.note: back means the whole assembly is read from right to left
held means the word is is grasped inside the phrase

parts.note: a daring trapeze artist performs with no net
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trapeze artist's dangerous wish is holding the crowd in suspense.
explanation.walkthrough: IS held inside NO NET makes NOISNET, which read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is stress or strain, as in a stretched rope or a tense moment.

clue.text: You and yours have reportedly stolen W. King's toys

indicators.note: stolen means certain letters are taken away from the two words

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
W is said as double U, that is two Us
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: You and your family are said to have pinched the toys of a Mr W King.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' tells us to hear W as 'double U'. Take two Us and R out of YOU YOURS to leave YO YOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Yo-yos are spinning toys that run up and down on a string.

clue.text: Down-to-earth in the exchanges?

parts.note: something as low as dirt in the marketplace, where trading is done, is very inexpensive

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down-to-earth' suggests a modest person; read it as priced as low as earth itself on the markets.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirt cheap means extremely inexpensive, priced as low as soil.

clue.text: In new term make drawer, adding colour

indicators.note: in says the word for make goes inside the reworked letters
new signals the word term is made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: a make of car is its brand

explanation.surface: In the new school term, an art pupil learns to draw and then add colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' looks like furniture but means someone who draws; 'In' puts the brand inside the reworked term.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt was the Dutch master who drew and painted, a draughtsman who added colour.

clue.text: Business deprived of drink? It's delivered earlier than the milk

definitions.text: It's delivered earlier than the milk

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
deprived of something means having lost it
rum is a drink

explanation.surface: A firm is denied its liquor and the milkman calls even earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' suggests a milkman's round; it is the first fluid a mother produces after giving birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Colostrum is the first secretion of the mammary glands after birth, before true milk comes in.

clue.text: Do in non-professional — in a few words

indicators.note: in puts the word for do inside the word for non-professional

parts.note: laic means lay, not of the clergy or a profession
to do someone is to con them

explanation.surface: Someone tells an amateur to swindle somebody, and to be brief about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech is terse, using few words, after the famously brief Spartans of Laconia.

clue.text: Health-promoting therapy's hard for a dog

indicators.note: hard for a means the letter for hard replaces the a

parts.note: shiatzu, or shiatsu, is a Japanese massage therapy promoting health
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A health-giving massage proves a bit hard on the family pet.
explanation.walkthrough: SHIATZU is a variant spelling of shiatsu; swap its A for H.
explanation.definitionFit: The shih-tzu is a small long-haired dog breed from Tibet and China.

clue.text: Chief of executives welcomed by French dish in the fold

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in by the French dish

parts.note: plat is French for a dish

indicators.note: chief of means the leading letter of executives

explanation.surface: A top executive is greeted with a French meal and brought into the fold.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold pressed into cloth.

clue.text: Possibly Sir Galahad or his film double is taking notice

indicators.note: is taking means the actor's name takes in the notice

parts.note: Michael Palin played Sir Galahad in Monty Python and the Holy Grail
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A knight's screen stand-in is paying attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking notice' looks like a phrase meaning paying attention; 'is taking' is the container signal. You need to know Monty Python's Holy Grail casting.
explanation.definitionFit: Galahad was a knight of the Round Table, and a paladin is a heroic knightly champion.

clue.text: One-time recidivist holds up this anti-social individual

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the held letters are read bottom to top
holds means the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: A former repeat offender is supporting a loner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-time recidivist' holds ETIMERE, which read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a religious hermit, someone who shuns society.

clue.text: Function of arsenic that's criminal

indicators.note: a criminal use of the word arsenic jumbles its letters

explanation.surface: A poisoner discusses the role of arsenic, which is illegal.
explanation.definitionFit: Arc sine is a trigonometric function, the inverse of the sine.

clue.text: Fragrant stuff — that's honey stored up the hill

indicators.note: up the hill means climbing, so in a down clue the letters read bottom to top
stored means the honey is kept inside the abbreviation

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is
mel is Latin for honey, used in pharmacy

explanation.surface: Something sweet-smelling, honey say, is kept up on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: MEL stored in IE gives IMELE, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin used in varnishes and perfumes.

clue.text: Fib about turning round style of artwork

indicators.note: round means the turned word goes around the fib
turning means the word for about is reversed

parts.note: about, as in argue about, means over
a fib is a lie

explanation.surface: A liar spins a tale about an art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the word for about, and 'round' wraps the result around the fib.
explanation.definitionFit: Relievo, or relief, is a sculptural style where figures project from a flat background.

clue.text: River spot in which I'll get lost, say? No circumnavigating Backs

indicators.note: going round and back means the whole thing is read in reverse
in puts the spot inside the abbreviation for say

parts.note: e.g., for example, means say

indicators.note: the letter I is lost from the spot

parts.note: a zit is a spot
nay means no

explanation.surface: A punter on the Cambridge river worries about getting lost on the way round the Backs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which I'll get lost' drops I from the spot, 'in' puts what remains inside 'say', and 'circumnavigating Backs' turns the lot round. The Backs are riverside college lawns in Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia, flowing across China.

clue.text: Big Ears? Yes, but not a close mate

definitions.meaning: Big Ears is the gnome friend of Noddy, a British children's book character, so a Noddy-ing companion
someone known only slightly, enough to nod to

explanation.walkthrough: Noddy is Enid Blyton's little wooden boy in British children's books; Big Ears is his friend, hence a 'Noddy-ing' pal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nodding acquaintance is a person you know only slightly, so far from a close friend.
